Scholarships for AI Graduate Students in Canada — Grokipedia Fact-checked by Grok 3 months ago Scholarships for AI Graduate Students in Canada Ara Eve Leo Sal 1x Scholarships for AI graduate students in Canada encompass a range of publicly available funding opportunities designed specifically for master's and PhD candidates pursuing studies in artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and related fields at Canadian universities, with eligibility often tied to AI-specific research criteria such as advancements in machine learning algorithms or AI applications in sectors like health and data science, distinguishing these from broader graduate funding programs. [1] [2] [3] These scholarships, active as of the 2025-2026 academic year, aim to attract and retain top domestic and international talent to bolster Canada's AI ecosystem, which is recognized for its contributions to innovation and economic growth through institutions like the Vector Institute and university-affiliated AI research centers. [1] [4] Notable examples include the Vector Scholarship in Artificial Intelligence , a $17,500 entrance award for exceptional students entering AI master's programs at Ontario universities, nominated by programs and providing access to networking with over 960 researchers and industry partners. [1] Another key program is the RBC Borealis Fellowships , offering $10,000 stipends to outstanding PhD students in ML or AI at any Canadian university, with selections emphasizing strong research proposals and diversity from underrepresented groups, alongside opportunities for co-publications and conference support. [2] Provincial and institutional initiatives further expand these opportunities; for instance, Alberta Innovates provides graduate student scholarships ranging from $12,000 to $31,000 annually for full-time research in emerging technologies including AI-related areas like information and communications technologies , available to students at Alberta institutions on a continuous intake basis . [3] Similarly, the Waterloo AI Institute Graduate Scholarship awards $5,000 to full-time graduate students at the University of Waterloo conducting AI or data science research under affiliated supervisors. [4] These programs foster AI talent development while prioritizing criteria like academic excellence, research potential, and alignment with Canada's national priorities in AI innovation. [1] [2] Overview Importance of Scholarships in AI Education Scholarships play a pivotal role in advancing artificial intelligence (AI) education at the graduate level in Canada, where the demand for AI expertise is rapidly expanding due to its applications in key sectors such as healthcare and autonomous systems. This growing need is driven by AI's potential to transform industries, with projections indicating significant economic contributions; for instance, a 2025 study estimates that AI has generated up to $100 billion in economic impact across Canada from 2019 to 2024, with projections of an additional $298 billion from 2025 to 2035, by fostering innovations in these areas. [5] Such demand underscores the importance of targeted funding to cultivate skilled researchers and professionals capable of addressing complex challenges in AI-driven technologies. The Pan-Canadian AI Strategy, launched in 2017, exemplifies how scholarships support the attraction of international talent and the retention of domestic students by providing essential financial resources for advanced studies. This strategy, developed in partnership with organizations like CIFAR , aims to position Canada as a global leader in AI by funding graduate programs that build world-class research capacity and top-tier talent. [6] By alleviating financial barriers, these scholarships enable students to focus on innovative research without the burden of excessive debt, thereby enhancing Canada's competitiveness in the global AI landscape. [7] Canada's AI job market has seen substantial growth, with AI-related job postings surging from 4,000 in 2012 to 57,000 in 2024, reflecting a fifteenfold increase and highlighting the urgent need for a robust talent pipeline. [8] Scholarships bridge critical financial gaps for graduate students pursuing AI studies, allowing them to engage fully in high-impact research amid rising living costs and tuition fees. This support is particularly vital in light of historical federal investments, which totaled $125 million starting in 2017 to initiate the Pan-Canadian AI Strategy and spur a marked increase in AI funding nationwide. [9] Programs such as the Vector Scholarship and RBC Borealis Fellowships illustrate the tangible impact of such initiatives in nurturing AI talent. General Eligibility Requirements Most scholarships for AI graduate students in Canada , as of 2025, require applicants to be enrolled full-time in a master's or PhD program focused on artificial intelligence or related fields at an eligible Canadian university. [10] [11] A minimum academic standing is typically expected, such as a GPA of 3.7/4.3 (equivalent to 80% or A- average) in the last two years of undergraduate or prior graduate study . [12] [4] Eligibility regarding citizenship often prioritizes Canadian citizens, permanent residents , or protected persons, though international students may qualify for select programs depending on the funding source. [13] [14] Programs commonly emphasize research in AI subfields, including machine learning, computer vision, natural language processing, or AI applications in various sectors. [2] Applicants must demonstrate potential for impactful AI research, often through a proposal outlining innovative contributions in these domains. [2] [11] Additional requirements frequently include letters of recommendation from academic or professional references attesting to the applicant's research aptitude, as well as a research proposal that aligns with AI innovation goals. [2] For non-native speakers, proof of proficiency in English or French is generally required, in line with university admission standards. Many scholarships incorporate diversity considerations to support underrepresented groups , such as women in AI, Indigenous students , visible minorities , or those from socioeconomically disadvantaged backgrounds, aiming to foster inclusive AI research communities. [15] [2] For instance, programs like the Canada Graduate Scholarships apply these general criteria while encouraging applications from diverse candidates. [16] Government-Funded Scholarships Canada Graduate Scholarships - Master's Program The Canada Graduate Scholarships - Master's (CGS M) program is a key federal funding initiative jointly administered by Canada's three primary research granting agencies: the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council (NSERC), the Canadian Institutes of Health Research (CIHR) , and the Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council (SSHRC) . Designed to support high-caliber master's students engaged in research, the program offers $27,000 for 12 months of full-time study, non-renewable, and aims to award up to 3,298 scholarships annually across various disciplines. [13] These awards help cover tuition and living expenses, enabling recipients to focus on innovative research without financial strain. For graduate students pursuing artificial intelligence (AI), eligibility is particularly relevant under the NSERC stream, which funds research in natural sciences and engineering fields, including AI applications such as machine learning algorithms, robotics, and data science methodologies. Applicants must propose a research project that aligns with these areas, demonstrating a significant autonomous research component, such as a thesis involving AI-driven analysis or modeling. [17] The program has supported various AI-related endeavors, for example, master's projects exploring robotic systems for environmental monitoring or data science techniques for predictive analytics in healthcare. [13] This focus ensures that AI students can access funding tailored to their interdisciplinary research needs. Applications for the CGS M are typically due by December 1 each year, submitted through the Research Portal to the applicant's chosen institution, which then conducts the merit review. Selection criteria emphasize academic excellence (50% weight), research potential (30% weight), and personal characteristics and interpersonal skills (20% weight), with evaluations considering factors like transcripts, research proposals , and leadership experience. [13] The competition is highly selective. [13] Successful AI applicants often highlight the novelty and feasibility of their proposed work in advancing fields like ethical AI or computational intelligence . This federal award can also be paired with provincial supplements to enhance overall funding. [13] Provincial and Territorial Programs Provincial and territorial programs in Canada offer targeted funding for AI graduate students, reflecting regional priorities such as innovation in emerging technologies , economic diversification, and local industry needs. These scholarships often complement federal awards like the Canada Graduate Scholarships - Master's (CGS M) by allowing stacking to support comprehensive research funding. Unlike uniform national programs, provincial initiatives vary in eligibility, value, and focus, with applications typically requiring endorsement from academic supervisors and alignment with AI-related research areas like machine learning or data-enabled innovations. [3] [18] In Alberta, the Alberta Innovates Graduate Student Scholarships program supports full-time master's and doctoral students conducting research in key emerging technology areas, including artificial intelligence, machine learning, and data science. Awards range from $12,000 to $31,000 per year for terms of one to four years, with a focus on priorities like energy-AI intersections to drive provincial economic growth. Applicants must secure supervisor endorsement and demonstrate academic excellence in AI-related fields. [3] [19] [20] Nova Scotia's Graduate Scholarship program provides merit-based funding for master's and PhD students engaged in innovative research, with AI projects eligible under themes of technological advancement and knowledge creation. For master's students, awards are valued at up to $10,000 per year for two years, while PhD recipients can receive up to $15,000 annually for four years, through an annual competition managed at the university level . This program emphasizes regional innovation, supporting AI applications in sectors like ocean technology and health sciences . [21] [22] In Ontario , the Ontario Graduate Scholarship (OGS) offers $15,000 awards to master's and doctoral students across disciplines, including AI-focused research. Administered provincially but applied through universities, OGS prioritizes academic merit and research potential, often aligning with Ontario's AI ecosystem strengths in urban centers. [23] [24] Quebec 's Fonds de recherche du Québec - Nature et technologies (FRQNT) provides substantial support for AI graduate research through programs like master's training scholarships valued at $20,000 per year for up to two years and doctoral scholarships at $21,000 annually for up to four years, totaling over $25,000 in many cases. These awards target natural sciences and engineering, explicitly including AI impacts on fields like documentary sciences and engineering innovations , with a focus on Quebec's bilingual research environment and industry partnerships. Regional differences are evident, as Alberta 's program underscores resource-sector AI applications, while Quebec emphasizes foundational AI advancements in technology and health .
